children: Microsoft (MSFT) reported fiscal first-quarter revenue of $92.3 billion, up 19% year over year, and diluted EPS of $4.92, up 32%. Azure revenue rose 48%; revenue and EPS beat forecasts.
Microsoft said some GPU-related cloud contracts shifted to the first half of 2027, affecting Azure growth timing. Quarterly capital spending and finance leases totaled $45.2 billion.
Bloomberg reports Microsoft (MSFT) is phasing out rented AI computing capacity from Oracle and declined to renew its agreement, citing changing requirements and older-generation Nvidia hardware.
Microsoft (MSFT) spent about $5 billion less than planned on Q3 capital expenditures as third-party data center delays, including an Iren project in Texas, postponed spending.
Microsoft (MSFT) is reviewing some third-party AI cloud providers and plans to prioritize capacity at its own data centers. It has not decided which providers it may drop.
Microsoft (MSFT) withdrew from an Nscale AI computing site in England, citing the provider’s electricity access, and reportedly won’t renew its Texas contract.
Microsoft reportedly delayed about $5 billion in planned spending after a customer-requested network upgrade pushed IREN’s Texas site launch to January or February.
Microsoft (MSFT) joined Amazon, Alphabet, Meta and Oracle in raising over $370.7 billion through U.S. investment-grade bonds this year, with borrowing used to fund AI investments.
Microsoft Corporation (MSFT) withdrew from a proposed data center project in the United Kingdom after infrastructure delays.
Microsoft Corporation (MSFT) is borrowing to finance AI data-center construction.
